headline: The EU's digital chief says Europe must avoid risky dependence on outside suppliers for AI, chips and other critical technology.
score_reason: Curator score kept; facts are statements of intent from one official, not new rules.
importance_line: What changed: the Commission's digital chief set out reducing outside dependence as a top goal for AI, quantum, chips, space and cybersecurity, which affects European governments and companies that buy from US or Chinese suppliers, but it is a stated aim without new measures.
summary: MLex reports that European Commission digital chief Henna Virkkunen says the EU must avoid "risky dependencies" in critical technologies such as AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, space and cyber security. European Newsroom, which also quotes her on Friday, adds that she wants the Union to avoid relying on a single company or third country for such technologies, and says the Commission has already sent formal requests for information to OpenAI, Anthropic and unnamed Chinese companies.
notes: Desk-built entry from MLex (paywalled; public description only) and European Newsroom (read in full); source label AI News Desk names both. Link is the MLex original; text read at europeannewsroom.com.
